To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diabetes causes an increase in the proportion of ribosomes in dimeric form, which is accompanied by a decrease in the ability of ribosomes to synthesize protein.
Chronic diabetes results in a decrease in the ability of rat liver ribosome populations to synthesize protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of diabetes on protein synthesis.
the effects of diabetes on the ribosome population and the activity of ribosomal protein synthetic systems in rat liver.
the effect of diabetes and insulin on the protein synthesizing system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

diabetes and insulin treatment of rats result in alterations in polysome populations, in ribosomal protein synthetic activity and in ribosomal structure, all of which are reversible by insulin treatment.

diabetes results in a decrease in the protein synthesizing activity of ribosomes and this change is due in part to a decrease in the number of active polysomes and a change in their magnesium sensitivity.
the ribosome from diabetic liver has an increased ability to initiate polypeptide synthesis and a decreased ability to form polysomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the changes in polysomal profiles and ribosome activity which occur as a result of the induction of diabetes in the rat are due to a decrease in the number of ribosomes which are actively engaged in the synthesis of protein.
diabetes results in the production of ribosomes which are less active in protein synthesis and more susceptible to dissociate to subunits than are those from control animals.
the protein synthetic activity and the polysome profile of the ribosomes of diabetic animals are altered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein synthesis machinery is altered in the diabetic state and is responsive to the insulin status of the animal.
ribosomes from diabetic rat livers have an enhanced capacity to synthesize protein in a cell-free assay system.
diabetes results in the presence of a significant amount of protein synthesis in a cell-free environment.
